title: Synthesis and characterization of Ru@PCN@PEI nanoparticles with catalytic activity
author: Wang, Chen, et al.

steps.title: Dialyze Ru nanoparticle suspension
steps.instruction: Transfer the Ru NP suspension into a pre‑rinsed 20 kDa dialysis bag (fill ≤ ½ of the bag capacity), place the bag in a beaker with excess DI water protected from light, and dialyze for 4 days, replacing the external DI water 3–4 times per day (optional: shorten to 2–3 days by changing water 6–8 times per day).

steps.title: Centrifuge and collect Ru NP pellet
steps.instruction: Collect the dialyzed solution, transfer it to a 50 mL centrifuge tube and centrifuge at 15,292 × g (12,000 rpm) at 4 °C for 30 min; discard the supernatant and keep the pellet.

steps.title: Freeze and lyophilize Ru nanoparticles
steps.instruction: Freeze the pellet at –80 °C for 12–16 h, then lyophilize at a condenser temperature of –60 °C under vacuum pressure < 15 Pa for 2–3 days to obtain a fine black Ru NP powder.

steps.title: Aliquot and store Ru NP powder
steps.instruction: Aliquot the powder into microcentrifuge (EP) tubes, label, and store protected from light; before use, sonicate in DI water for ≤ 10 min (recommended 3 min) to obtain a deep‑black suspension.

steps.title: Centrifuge Ru@PCN product
steps.instruction: Transfer the Ru@PCN product solution to a 50 mL centrifuge tube, centrifuge at 15,292 × g (12,000 rpm) at 4 °C for 30 min, discard the supernatant and retain the pellet.

steps.title: Perform three DMF washes
steps.instruction: Add sufficient DMF to the pellet, sonicate for 3 min, centrifuge at 15,292 × g, 4 °C, 30 min and discard the supernatant; repeat this wash a total of three times, inverting the tube immediately after each spin to avoid pellet dissolution.

steps.title: Water wash and disperse Ru@PCN
steps.instruction: Add DI water to cover the pellet, sonicate for 5 min, let stand for 2 h, then centrifuge (15,292 × g, 4 °C, 30 min) and discard the supernatant; subsequently add 10 mL DI water and sonicate 5 min to obtain a uniform dispersion.

steps.title: Dialyze Ru@PCN dispersion
steps.instruction: Transfer the dispersion to a 100 kDa dialysis bag (fill ≤ ½ bag volume), place the bag in a 1 L beaker containing 600 mL DI water with a magnetic stir bar, stir at 600 rpm and dialyze for 4 days, replacing the external DI water 3–4 times per day; ensure the bag and clamp are airtight.

steps.title: Pre‑cool and lyophilize Ru@PCN
steps.instruction: After dialysis, transfer the contents to a 50 mL centrifuge tube, centrifuge at 15,292 × g, 4 °C, 30 min and discard the supernatant; pre‑cool the pellet at 4 °C for 2 h, then at –20 °C for 5 h, and finally at –80 °C for 12–16 h; lyophilize for 2–3 days to obtain the final Ru@PCN powder.

steps.title: Centrifuge Ru@PCN@PEI suspension
steps.instruction: Transfer the Ru@PCN@PEI suspension to a 50 mL centrifuge tube, centrifuge at 15,292 × g (12,000 rpm) at 4 °C for 30 min, discard the supernatant and retain the pellet.

steps.title: Water washes to remove excess reagents
steps.instruction: Add 10 mL DI water to the pellet, sonicate for 3 min, then centrifuge (15,292 × g, 4 °C, 30 min) and discard the supernatant; repeat this centrifugation and DI‑water wash three times to eliminate unreacted PEI, EDC and NHS.

steps.title: Dialyze Ru@PCN@PEI dispersion
steps.instruction: Disperse the purified pellet in 10 mL DI water, transfer to a 100 kDa dialysis bag (≤ ½ bag volume), place in a 1 L beaker with 600 mL DI water, stir at 600 rpm for 4 days, and replace the external DI water 3–4 times per day.

steps.title: Pre‑cool and lyophilize Ru@PCN@PEI
steps.instruction: Transfer the dialysis contents to a 50 mL centrifuge tube, centrifuge at 15,292 × g, 4 °C, 30 min and discard the supernatant; pre‑cool the pellet at 4 °C for 2 h, then at –20 °C for 5 h, and finally at –80 °C for 12–16 h; lyophilize for 2–3 days to obtain the final Ru@PCN@PEI powder.

description: BMOFs combine the structural advantages of metal-organic frameworks with the catalytic activity of metal catalysts, offering great potential in mimicking the catalytic functions of natural enzymes.1 Studies have shown that PCN-222(Mn) nanoparticles (NPs) combines the stability of zirconium (Zr) and the high catalytic activity of manganese (Mn), exhibiting superoxide dismutase (SOD)-like activity.2 However, the current PCN-222(Mn) NPs prepared have relatively large particle sizes (>200 nm), which limits their application in the biomedical field.3,4 Therefore, controlling the particle size of PCN-222(Mn) and modifying it to enhance its SOD-like activity is of significant importance.5 This protocol describes the synthesis of Ru@PCN@PEI NPs with tunable particle size and superoxide dismutase (SOD)-like catalytic activity. The workflow includes the solvothermal synthesis of PCN-222(Mn) NPs with the aid of modulators to achieve the desired particle size, followed by in situ incorporation of Ru NPs to obtain Ru@PCN NPs, and a surface coating with polyethyleneimine (PEI). Although this work focuses on Ru NPs and PEI, the same principles can be extended to other metal species, framework compositions, and polymer coatings to guide the design of functional BMOF-based materials.
